content:
Logan Wright: heads up: incident-bot messages for perf-canary alerts are too big + not deduping well. Thread to iterate on formatting before we flip paging in us-east.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Oncall feedback from last week: same regression posts 6 threads b/c dedupe key changes when baseline window rolls. Also the payload is like a full page of numbers.

Allison Grant: yep. We need: (1) compact summary at top (2) stable dedupe key (3) actionable links (dash + runbook) (4) keep raw details collapsible.

Noah Patel: canary side can include `alert_id` if we decide on a deterministic hash. Right now we hash model+metric+region+tier+runtime_build, but baseline_version is included so it churns.

Nadia Rahman: don’t include baseline_version in the thread key. Baseline can change hourly if we’re doing rolling windows.

Caleb Johnson: also: please don’t paste full labels/series in the Slack message. The bot currently dumps the entire PromQL labelset in a code block; it’s noisy and can leak config values we don’t need.

Logan Wright: proposing dedupe key:
- `perf_canary` (source)
- env (prod)
- model_id (canonical)
- region
- metric (p95_e2e_ms / tokens_per_sec)
- runtime_version (or runtime_build)
- hw_sku (only if configured, otherwise omit)

Rafael Mendes: question: do we want runtime_version in dedupe? if we roll forward and it’s still bad, I’d prefer a new thread so it’s obvious it persisted across releases.

Allison Grant: agree. Dedupe should represent “same regression event context”. I’d include runtime_build (or release tag) + maybe kernel tag if stable.

Noah Patel: kernel tag is sometimes “auto” and then actual kernel changes under the hood. We added `kernel_selection_id` recently. That should be stable enough for RCA and thread separation.

Logan Wright: ok. Dedupe key v1:
`perfcanary|prod|{model_id}|{region}|{metric}|{runtime_build}|{kernel_selection_id}|{hw_sku}`
If any of those are missing, we use `unknown` so it’s stable.

Caleb Johnson: careful with hw_sku: can explode for some pools if it’s not normalized. Can we map to a small enum (A100-80G, H100-80G, L40S, etc)?

Nadia Rahman: yes, telemetry already has normalized `gpu_sku` dimension. Please use that, not raw instance type.

Rafael Mendes: also: summary needs severity + confidence + “sustained X mins” so oncall can decide quickly.

Allison Grant: and links:
- Grafana panel (pre-filtered)
- trace search (if applicable)
- runbook
- rollback checklist (optional, but at least point to runbook section)

Logan Wright: draft message format:

Top line:
`[PERF-CANARY][PAGE] llama-3.1-70b-instruct (us-east, hosted) p95 e2e latency +18% vs baseline (1.42s -> 1.68s), sustained 20m, n=640, confidence=high`

Then bullets:
- Breakdown: queue +35%, prefill +2%, decode +4% (if present)
- Runtime: redwood-runtime 2026.02.05.1 / kernel_selection_id=attn_v3_7
- GPU: H100-80G
- Baseline: baseline_id=llama-3.1-70b-instruct/us-east/H100/2026.02.01

Then links:
`Dashboard | Traces | Runbook`

Then “Details” code block with observed/baseline stats.

Rafael Mendes: looks good. One ask: move baseline_id out of the main bullets unless warning. It causes people to chase baseline drift. For paging we should bias toward “is it real now?” and “what changed?”

Allison Grant: +1. Baseline id can be in details.

Noah Patel: canary can also include a “suspected attribution” field if we detect queueing dominates (scheduler) vs runtime-only (kernel). But we should label it as heuristic.

Caleb Johnson: yes but keep it short, like `Likely: queueing (scheduler/capacity)` vs `Likely: execution (kernel/runtime)`.

Logan Wright: ok.

Nadia Rahman: re: confidence: how computed? We should avoid a fake number.

Noah Patel: current evaluator returns a discrete bucket: low/med/high based on min samples + variance vs baseline. Not a p-value. We can rename `confidence` -> `signal_strength`.

Allison Grant: please do. “confidence” reads like stats.

Rafael Mendes: +1 rename.

Logan Wright: ack. `signal_strength=high`.

Caleb Johnson: also: please include `alert_fingerprint` (the dedupe key) in the details so we can search logs when Slack does weird stuff.

incident-bot: (example output - current)
"Perf Canary Regression Detected\nmodel=llama-3.1-70b-instruct\nmetric=p95_e2e_ms\nlabels={model_id=..., region=..., tier=..., runtime_build=..., baseline_version=..., prompt_bucket=..., seed=..., ...}\nobserved_histogram=...\nbaseline_histogram=...\n..." 

Rafael Mendes: yeah this is the firehose I was talking about :grimacing:

Allison Grant: we should *not* include prompt_bucket/seed in Slack. That’s internal canary config. Keep it out of the bot message and out of dedupe.

Noah Patel: agreed. Those labels are for metrics, but Slack should show only the “debug set”.

Logan Wright: proposal: add allowlist for fields rendered into Slack. Everything else stays in event JSON in our logs, not posted.

Caleb Johnson: +1 allowlist.

Nadia Rahman: make sure we’re not posting raw URLs with query params that include internal IDs. Grafana links should be short / use variables.

Logan Wright: yep, using the shared “short link” endpoint that generates a stable URL without long query strings.

Rafael Mendes: what about threads: 1 alert = 1 thread. Updates should reply in-thread with “still firing” at some interval? Not every minute.

Allison Grant: for warning: update every 30m. for paging: update every 10-15m max. and stop after resolved.

Logan Wright: we already have a dampener in incident-bot. I’ll tune:
- page: post update at 15m intervals while firing
- warn: 45m
- resolution message once cleared for 10m

Noah Patel: also: don’t auto-resolve if metrics ingestion lags. We saw that during the telemetry pipeline delay.

Caleb Johnson: yup. Add “data freshness” check: only resolve if last datapoint < 5m old.

Logan Wright: ok.

deploy-bot: Logan Wright pushed a commit to incident-bot (branch: perf-canary-formatting)

Logan Wright: implemented:
- new Block Kit layout (header + summary + links)
- allowlist fields
- dedupe fingerprint change (removed baseline_version, prompt_bucket, seed)
- details collapsed into a single code block (max 20 lines)

PR going out in ~10m.

Rafael Mendes: can you paste the new preview here?

Logan Wright: 
`[PERF-CANARY][WARN] mistral-large-2 (eu-west, dedicated) tokens/sec -12% vs baseline (820 -> 722), sustained 45m, n=480, signal_strength=med`
• Likely: queueing/capacity (queue_ms +28%)
• Runtime: 2026.02.05.1 | Kernel: attn_v3_7 | GPU: A100-80G
Links: Dashboard | Runbook | Incident timeline
Details:
```
fingerprint=perfcanary|prod|mistral-large-2|eu-west|tokens_per_sec|2026.02.05.1|attn_v3_7|A100-80G
observed: p50=..., p95=..., tps=722
baseline: tps=820 (window=7d)
min_samples: ok (>=400)
data_freshness: 2m
```

Allison Grant: looks much better. One nit: “Incident timeline” link might confuse folks if it’s a warning. Maybe label it “Alert history”?

Rafael Mendes: +1 rename to Alert history.

Nadia Rahman: baseline window in details is good. If window changes per model, please render actual policy (fixed vs rolling) to avoid future confusion.

Noah Patel: we can include `baseline_policy=rolling_7d` in details.

Logan Wright: will do.

Caleb Johnson: and cap the code block to avoid >4k characters. Looks ok now.

Logan Wright: cool. I’ll update labels and merge once CI is green.

Rafael Mendes: thanks. Once merged, we can re-run a synthetic warning in #incidents to verify dedupe + links.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: pls also add runbook section anchor in the runbook link ("#triage-perf-canary-alert") so folks jump to the right spot.

Logan Wright: good call, adding anchor.

Noah Patel: after merge, I’ll update perf-canary webhook payload doc to match the new field names (signal_strength, fingerprint, etc.).

Rafael Mendes: :+1:
